purpose: Test whether the RC20 peak-RIR reduction transports without retraining from calibration mixtures 1a-1c to official compositions 1d-1h, and preregister a full-pattern empirical reference competitor that uses the same calibration and untouched holdouts.

frozenPeakReduction.contract: Inherit response-ratio estimation, primary and secondary centers, signal and sideband widths, linear background, positive trapezoid area, refusal rule, and five-point unsafe definition verbatim from IUCR-QPA-INDEPENDENT-PEAK-RIR-0.1.
frozenPeakReduction.noRetuning: Do not change any peak parameter or response ratio after loading 1d-1h, and do not use 1d-1h to select a gate.

preregisteredFullPatternCompetitor.baseline: Partition the full original 5-150 degree grid into consecutive 2-degree bins; take the fifth percentile count and median angle per bin; linearly interpolate these anchors over every point; subtract and clip at zero. Use the resulting 20-100 degree segment without resampling.
preregisteredFullPatternCompetitor.templates: Use the baseline-subtracted pure corundum, fluorite, and zincite profiles as three fixed nonnegative columns on their common grid.
preregisteredFullPatternCompetitor.coefficientFit: Solve unweighted nonnegative least squares by enumerating all seven nonempty active phase sets and ordinary least squares within each set; reject singular or negative active coefficients and choose minimum squared residual.
preregisteredFullPatternCompetitor.responseCalibration: For each calibration mixture 1a-1c, fit coefficients c_sk. Against fluorite compute log[(c_sk/c_s,fluorite)/(W_sk/W_s,fluorite)] and take the median for each non-fluorite phase; set fluorite response to one.
preregisteredFullPatternCompetitor.weightEstimate: For every target set u_k=c_k/r_k and normalize positive u values to 100 weight percent. Refuse if any phase coefficient or calibrated response is non-positive.
preregisteredFullPatternCompetitor.residual: Report square root of residual sum of squares divided by target baseline-subtracted L2 norm. The residual is diagnostic and cannot alter the five-point truth gate.

competingHypotheses.claim: The frozen RC20 primary peak-RIR transports to all five untouched compositions.
competingHypotheses.prediction: All five 1d-1h profiles are estimable and maximum phase error is at most five weight-percentage points for every profile.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: Any holdout is refused or exceeds five points.

competingHypotheses.claim: The preregistered full-pattern empirical reference reduction transports to all five untouched compositions.
competingHypotheses.prediction: All five profiles are estimable and maximum phase error is at most five points for every profile.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: Any holdout is refused or exceeds five points.

competingHypotheses.claim: Using the whole pattern materially reduces the peak method's worst holdout error without sacrificing estimability.
competingHypotheses.prediction: The full-pattern maximum error is at least 20% lower than the primary-peak maximum error, with five of five profiles estimable.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: The reduction is below 20%, a profile is refused, or the full-pattern worst error exceeds five points.

competingHypotheses.claim: Primary-secondary peak disagreement ranks external composition error strongly enough to prioritize method review.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Across five holdouts, Spearman correlation between peak-family disagreement and primary maximum error is at least 0.8 without a negative tie ambiguity.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: Correlation is below 0.8 or cannot be computed.

decisionRules.primaryTruth: Use official weighed values for the five-point gate; report the official XRF values separately as a different measurement principle and do not blend them into a tuned target.
decisionRules.safety: One refused or unsafe composition rejects method-wide transport. Average error cannot rescue a failing composition.
decisionRules.comparison: Report every phase estimate, phase error, refusal, residual, and method disagreement before any aggregate.
decisionRules.promotion: Passing five historical profiles does not qualify physical independence or an arbitrary new instrument.

uncertaintyBudget: Each holdout is one historical profile, so counting variation and preparation variation are not separately estimated.

Archive replay may change transport bytes and some archived angles print up to 0.00001 degree below their nominal values; deterministic count-preserving nominal-grid normalization and current official grid cross-check protect numerical lineage but do not recreate collection metadata.
Peak background is vulnerable to local tails; full-pattern percentile background is vulnerable to broad amorphous or unresolved intensity.
Pure-reference patterns and mixtures may differ in packing, orientation, absorption, crystallinity, and incident intensity.
Weighed and XRF values have different error sources, but neither supplies a prospective two-institution repeat.
stopConditions: Stop if any numerical file differs from 7,251 points or any printed angle lies more than 0.00002 degree from the 5+0.02*i nominal grid.
Stop and preserve the failure if a required phase area, coefficient, or response is non-positive.
Do not change preprocessing, calibration, truth, hypotheses, or gates after computing any 1d-1h estimate.
Do not call a historical same-instrument holdout an independent physical replication.
